evidence.claim: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.title: NEDA to flesh out development agenda for addressing constraints to inclusive growth
evidence.excerpt: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official release quoting NEDA's implementation agenda and priorities.
contrary_evidence: It is an agenda statement, not implementation.
The source is official and promotional.

evidence.claim: Marcos's economic managers said the 8-point socioeconomic agenda aimed to cut poverty to 9 percent by the end of the six-year term and raise the Philippines to upper-middle-income status by 2028.
evidence.title: PH socioeconomic agenda presented at IMF, World Bank meeting
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's economic managers said the 8-point socioeconomic agenda aimed to cut poverty to 9 percent by the end of the six-year term and raise the Philippines to upper-middle-income status by 2028.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and agenda bullet list
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated report on official targets announced by the administration.
contrary_evidence: The source is a government newswire.

evidence.claim: DSWD said updated AICS guidelines expedited aid by simplifying intake and eligibility forms, shortening procedures, and increasing beneficiaries served.
evidence.title: Request for assistance under AICS now easier for clients
evidence.publisher: Department of Social Welfare and Development
evidence.excerpt: DSWD said updated AICS guidelines expedited aid by simplifying intake and eligibility forms, shortening procedures, and increasing beneficiaries served.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 agency announcement with specific procedural changes and implementation effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level attribution is partial; the reform was implemented by DSWD under Secretary Tulfo, within the Marcos administration.
contrary_evidence: This is an implementation reform, not a measured welfare outcome.
The article attributes the directive to the secretary rather than Marcos personally.

evidence.claim: DepEd issued School Year 2022-2023 guidelines committing to the resumption of five-day in-person classes, with ALS beginning at school opening and BEDP 2030 and the Learning Recovery and Continuity Plan guiding implementation.
evidence.title: DepEd releases guidelines for School Year 2022-2023
evidence.excerpt: DepEd issued School Year 2022-2023 guidelines committing to the resumption of five-day in-person classes, with ALS beginning at school opening and BEDP 2030 and the Learning Recovery and Continuity Plan guiding implementation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated official policy with explicit school-opening and ALS provisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level attribution is partial; DepEd led the measure under VP-Secretary Sara Duterte within the Marcos administration.
contrary_evidence: The policy was executed by DepEd rather than Marcos personally.
It reflects recovery from pandemic disruption more than a new social-welfare architecture.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said its Philippines work from April to September 2022 included accelerating learning recovery, bringing child protection services closer through TeleCPUs, and building a more equitable world through digital public goods.
evidence.title: For every child, results - Issue 3
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said its Philippines work from April to September 2022 included accelerating learning recovery, bringing child protection services closer through TeleCPUs, and building a more equitable world through digital public goods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Bulletin-style report with a dated coverage window and concrete program themes, though not a ruler-specific audit.
evidence.period_fit: April to September 2022 coverage within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect; useful as evidence of the welfare service environment under the Marcos administration, not of direct presidential authorship.
contrary_evidence: This is a UNICEF summary, not a Marcos performance evaluation.
It aggregates partner work across multiple actors.

evidence.claim: UNICEF described a child with cerebral palsy in Southern Leyte whose care and nutrition were disrupted by Typhoon Odette, damaged housing, and blocked roads, illustrating how disasters worsened access for vulnerable families.
evidence.title: Supporting Most Vulnerable Children to Fight Malnutrition in Southern Leyte
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF described a child with cerebral palsy in Southern Leyte whose care and nutrition were disrupted by Typhoon Odette, damaged housing, and blocked roads, illustrating how disasters worsened access for vulnerable families.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct case-based reporting with a clear vulnerability and disaster-access narrative.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect crisis context; not a direct Marcos action, but relevant to the vulnerability baseline his administration inherited and faced.
contrary_evidence: This is a humanitarian case study, not a ruler-attribution finding.
The article does not test government program effectiveness directly.

evidence.claim: DHSUD said ESAP would be improved under Marcos directives with better coordination with DSWD, providing calamity-affected families emergency cash assistance or construction materials to repair damaged houses.
evidence.title: DHSUD one with Marcos admin in boosting disaster response ops
evidence.excerpt: DHSUD said ESAP would be improved under Marcos directives with better coordination with DSWD, providing calamity-affected families emergency cash assistance or construction materials to repair damaged houses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire reporting a specific presidential directive and program change, with direct policy detail.
contrary_evidence: The delivery mechanism remained DHSUD/DSWD-led rather than personally presidential.
This is shelter relief, not a full welfare-system evaluation.

evidence.claim: NEDA said the national ID system would strengthen monitoring for social protection distribution, and the government was using fuel subsidies for drivers, farmers, and fisherfolk to cushion price shocks.
evidence.title: Marcos admin ensures continued economic recovery from pandemic
evidence.excerpt: NEDA said the national ID system would strengthen monitoring for social protection distribution, and the government was using fuel subsidies for drivers, farmers, and fisherfolk to cushion price shocks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official-government newswire with a detailed, dated report on administration measures and implementation path.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct administration-level attribution, though several measures were inherited or jointly managed across agencies.
contrary_evidence: The report frames measures as recovery management, not durable welfare transformation.
Some components, such as the national ID, were already in motion before Marcos.

evidence.claim: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that the administration would raise production to counter food-price spikes and support purchasing power.
evidence.title: Marcos relays food production agenda in 1st SONA
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that the administration would raise production to counter food-price spikes and support purchasing power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement published by the implementing department with concrete policy direction.
contrary_evidence: The claim is a policy direction, not a delivery outcome.
Food-price pressure was partly inherited and global.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
